Now that Typhoon Sinlaku is well north of Saipan, weather has calmed
down a bit. Breezy conditions look to continue for another day or so,
with a very dry pattern moving into the region. Only partly cloudy 
skies and isolated showers or light showers are expected through the
weekend and into next week. Fresh to strong winds look to become
light to gentle by Saturday night or Sunday.

Marine/Surf...
As TY Sinlaku continues to move away from the region, large northwest
swell along with moderate southwest swell will maintain hazardous
seas across Guam and Rota waters through Saturday afternoon morning 
and across Tinian and Saipan waters through Sunday morning. These 
large swell trains will continue to produce deadly surf and rip 
currents along south, west and north facing reefs of Guam and Rota 
tonight through Saturday morning along with moderate coastal flooding
of up to 2 feet for Guam and Rota. Surf and rip currents look to 
remain hazardous into Sunday afternoon. For Tinian and Saipan, 
significant coastal flooding of 3 to 5 feet will continue through 
early Saturday morning, with moderate coastal flooding up to 2 feet 
continuing through late Sunday morning. Combined seas of up to 21 
feet for northern Tinian and Saipan waters, and up to 18 feet for 
Guam and Rota, will slowly subside over the next couple of days, A 
Hazardous Seas Warning will continue into the weekend, along with a 
Small Craft Advisory, initially for winds, then for seas as the seas 
fall below 15 feet Saturday.

Tropical Systems...
Earlier this morning, Typhoon Warnings have been cancelled for Rota,
Tinian, and Saipan, but remain in effect for Alamagan, Pagan, and 
Agrihan in the CNMI and the adjacent coastal waters.

Typhoon Sinlaku continues to move through the far northern 
Mariana Islands. At 5pm this afternoon, Sinlaku was located near 
20.0N and 145.8E, about 95 miles north of Agrihan and about 345 
miles north of Saipan. It is now on the eastern side of the 
archipelago. Sinlaku is producing dense cloud cover and widespread 
showers over the far northern Marianas with weaker rainbands well to 
the south, across Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan. The eye is poorly 
defined and drier air is wrapping around to the west-southwest of its
center. Heaviest rainbands are focused along the eastern to northern
sides of the system. Sinlaku continues to weaken, now a Category 1 
typhoon with maximum sustained winds around 90 mph. Typhoon force 
winds extend outward from the center up to 85 miles. Tropical storm 
force winds extend outward from the center up to 270 miles to the 
northeast and up to 235 miles elsewhere. Sinlaku is moving northeast 
at 7 mph, it is expected to make a slight turn toward the north-
northeast with a slight increase in forward speed through Saturday. 
Typhoon force winds have moved north of Agrihan, although tropical 
storm force conditions remain through Saturday morning. Alamagan is 
expected to see tropical storm force conditions through late this 
evening or overnight. Pagan is expected to see tropical storm force 
conditions through tonight or early Saturday morning. As this 
weakening trend continues, along with its north-northeast trajectory,
Sinlaku may become extratropical sometime Sunday.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from
the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
An Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) fragment is interacting 
with a trade-wind trough traversing the ITCZ and generating an
unsettled pattern across central and southern RMI. The ITCZ is 
expected to continue to develop across eastern Micronesia and is 
expected to bring showers through the weekend at Majuro and through 
the middle of next week for Kosrae. Pohnpei can expect to see a few 
periods of shower through the middle of next week as the ITCZ is 
anticipated to stay to the south. 

Altimetry shows combined seas of 6 feet near Pohnpei and 4 to 5 near
Majuro. There are two mixed swells in the region at Pohnpei and 
Kosrae and one at Majuro. The first is a mix of west and northeast 
swells and the other is a mix of east and northeast swells. Winds are
expected to light to moderate through the middle of next week.

Western Micronesia...
A dry pattern has set up in the wake of Typhoon Sinlaku. Through the
middle of next week, isolated showers with a few periods of 
scattered showers can be expected with one caveat, around Monday 
showers may build to around 50 percent chance for Chuuk as the 
showers from Pohnpei may move through the region. 

The main concerns for the region are in the marine conditions around
Yap. Swell produced by Sinlaku are keeping the seas and surf

tide times with the new moon cycle adding to the surf heights. Seas
